The so-called Gag Rule seems to be misunderstood by some on @X.

The “rule” was an administrative policy adopted by the SEC as Rule 202.5(e). 
In practice, the Rule meant that the SEC, in its press release announcing a settlement, would say the settling company “neither admits nor denies” the factual allegations in the SEC’s complaint.

The settling company was not “gagged” but it had to stick to the “neither admits nor denies” formulation when talking about the settlement.
